speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; I need to understand the progression of your right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and recent memory issues. Can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they are getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline you described is concerning; the combination of one-week neurological decline and six months of cognitive and behavioral changes suggests an aggressive process. Given his age and the rapid onset of right leg weakness with falls, do you have any history of head trauma, recent infections, or exposure to toxins like heavy metals or solvents?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD). The rapid progression of dementia, myoclonus equivalents (falls/weakness), and behavioral changes in a 44-year-old male are highly suggestive of sporadic CJD. I request MRI Brain images immediately to look for the characteristic "cortical ribboning" or "pulvinar sign."
